final_answer: The Dead Sea is called "dead" because its extremely high salinity makes it nearly impossible for most aquatic life to survive. The extreme salinity results from a combination of geological and chemical factors. Minerals from surrounding rocks dissolve into the water, and because the Dead Sea has no natural outlet, water evaporates, leaving behind concentrated salts. Over time, this process has led to one of the highest salt concentrations in the world, creating an environment where only a few specialized organisms can exist.
